content.body:
The appearance in battle, and defensive quality of, the heavier Allied tanks like the Matilda and Char B1 bis was a surprise to some German designers at the time. Combat reports from battles just waged sent them immediately back to the drawing board to develop ways to mount better guns on their tanks. The Panzer IV was fortunately equipped with a large turret ring, making the mounting of the much longer (nearly double Panzer IV D's gun) 75 mm L43 AT gun a simple task.
This potent weapon, coupled with a front armor upgrade, made the Panzer IV G a solid performer and a successful tank throughout the rest of the war. The original thin armor on the sides and rear left it vulnerable to flank attacks, something that Allied AT gunners would continue to use to great effect. Due to the overall anti-armor lethality of this longer 75 mm gun, the Panzer IV G does not have the HEAT ammunition of its short-barreled ancestor seen in the previous Panzer IV D design.
The Panzer IV G became the mainstay of German armored units for the rest of the war for good reason: a highly useful combination of mobility, front armor, and an accurate and lethal main gun that can kill any Allied tank at significant ranges. Taken together, they make it an effective all-around weapon in any situation. Be sure to keep in mind that you have a tremendous range advantage and good quality sights. This is NOT the tank that you take down into the contested town - it is far too valuable for such a dubious role. You can sit at extended ranges, nearly impervious to return fire on your front, and annihilate any tank you see except the Churchills. Keep moving, firing, and relocating under cover wherever possible in order to minimize the ability of the enemy to focus ground or aerial resources effectively to eliminate you.
You will stand out as a particularly high-value target to Allied aircraft if they can spot you. Your commander is only useful if he is able to see so leave him unbuttoned most of the time (pull him in during air attack or if you are entering an urban area). If he is killed, the slight risk to your tank through his open hatch) will have been more than offset by his utility to that point if you used him to spot for you.
Move quickly from cover to cover, scanning carefully. Use shadows and brush to break up your outline as much as possible.
Control Variations: Gunner sight now has a fully-modeled multi-ammo sight; PzGr is the range for AP rounds, SprGr is the range setting for HE.
